method.returns: Daily total returns from dividend-adjusted closes on SPY's trading days (other markets carried forward up to 5 days), portfolio_lab.universe.load_all_returns. CASH = ^IRX / 100 / 252 each day (T-bill yield earned daily; yield carried forward over gaps). Funds quoted in SGD or GBP/GBp are converted to USD by the loader.
method.sgd: SGD daily return = (1 + USD daily return) x (1 + fx) - 1, fx = daily change of SGD=X (unhedged). No SGD result exists before 2003-12 (fx missing).

mix.start: A mix starts on the first day every chosen block has a daily return, and never before 2005-01-03 (model_portfolios.build). The window is sliced after building: mixes are NOT restarted at the window start (this matters only for where monthly rebalances fall relative to drift).
mix.rebalance_dates: The last trading day of each calendar month within the mix's own date range, including the final, partial month (2026-10-27 is a rebalance day): portfolio_lab.mix.month_ends(index).
algorithm: held = target weights (array summing to 1) on the start day, before that day's return
for each day i: grown_j = held_j x (1 + r_ij);  nav = sum_j grown_j;  ret_i = nav - 1;  held_j = grown_j / nav
if day i is a rebalance date: ret_i = ret_i - (sum_j |held_j - target_j|) x cost_bps / 10000 x (1 + ret_i);  then held = target
missing block returns inside the mix are treated as 0 (never happens in the shipped blocks after their start)
mix.simple_twin: fixed_mix of SPY (stock share) + CASH (rest), monthly, 5 bps, started 2005-01-03 (model_portfolios.build_simple).

method.window: Window 'since YYYY' = daily returns from the window's first day (2008-01-02, 2015-01-02, 2020-01-02) to 2026-10-27, both inclusive: the first day's own return counts (strategist and run_mix convention). Some team READMEs start from the next day (base close on the first day), so their figures can differ in the last digit (e.g. SPY since 2008: 11.2% here and in the strategist, 11.3% in defensive_equity).
method.explorer_window: A fund gets a window card only if it has a price on the window's first day and no gaps after. If its first daily return is the next trading day (price on the first day only), the first day's return counts as 0 (listed in the fund's first_day_zero).

scorecard.function: portfolio_lab.drawdowns.scorecard(returns) on the window's daily returns (n = number of days)
scorecard.drawdown: curve = cumprod(1 + r); dd = curve / max(running max of curve, 1.0) - 1  (the running max starts at 1, the value before the first day)
scorecard.f10: falls of 10%+: walk the days; a day with dd >= 0 ends the current episode (counted if its lowest dd was <= -0.10) and sets a new peak; an unrecovered episode at the end also counts (portfolio_lab.drawdowns.falls, threshold 0.10)
scorecard.wm: worst month = min over calendar months of prod(1 + r) - 1 (first and last months partial)
scorecard.luw: longest underwater = longest run of consecutive days with dd < 0, divided by 21 (months)
scorecard.ulcer: Ulcer index (pain) = sqrt(mean(dd^2)) over all days; shown x100 in the reports

same_pain_edge.function: portfolio_lab.mix.same_pain_edge(x, spy, cash) over the same window
same_pain_edge.line: 21 SPY + T-bill mixes rebalanced DAILY: r_w = w x r_SPY + (1 - w) x r_CASH for w = 0, 0.05, ..., 1; for each, (Ulcer index, CAGR) by the scorecard above; points sorted by (Ulcer, CAGR)
same_pain_edge.edge: edge = CAGR(x) - interp(Ulcer(x), line ulcers, line CAGRs); null when Ulcer(x) is above SPY's ('more pain than SPY'; numpy interp right = NaN). Below the first point interp returns the first CAGR (never happens in USD: 100% T-bills has Ulcer 0).
same_pain_edge.spy_share: SPY share of the same-pain mix: interp(Ulcer(x), Ulcer of 101 daily mixes w = 0, 0.01, ..., 1, w) (model_portfolios.same_share)
same_pain_edge.edge_sgd_proxy: SGD edge vs SPY (in SGD) + cash earning the US T-bill yield with no currency move (an approximate stand-in for SGD cash; no SGD rate is in the data): same_pain_edge on SGD series with safe = CASH in USD
same_pain_edge.edge_sgd_usbills: SGD edge vs SPY + US T-bills both seen in SGD (model_portfolios.edge_frontier: sorted 21-point line, interp with left = right = NaN; null = calmer than every such mix or more painful than SPY)
same_pain_edge.explorer: The explorer shows the USD edge only (as the teams did).

method.spy_falls: model_portfolios.spy_falls: falls of 10%+ of SPY over its whole history (portfolio_lab.drawdowns.falls) whose peak is on or after 2007-01-01, plus 'inner' falls of 10%+ that start after a fall's low and end before its old high is regained (2010, 2011). SGD set: the same on SPY in SGD from 2004-01-01. A series' result in a fall = portfolio_lab.drawdowns.return_over(x, peak, low) = prod(1 + r) over days after the peak up to and including the low; null if the series does not cover the whole span.

browser_tolerance.what: Largest difference between the full-precision reference metrics and the same metrics recomputed in Python from the rounded shipped arrays (what a browser re-implementation sees). Compare with a tolerance of about this plus 0.00005 (the 4-decimal rounding of checks).

schema.dates: Shared trading-day array (ISO strings) from 2005-01-03 to 2026-10-27, for blocks and fx.
schema.blocks: {id: {first, r}}: daily returns (6 decimals) of each builder block; r[k] is the return on dates[first + k]; no gaps after first. block_info[id] = {kind: research|ibkr, role, name, note, first_date}.
schema.fx: {first, r, what}: daily USD/SGD change on the same dates.
schema.checks: List of reference rows {id, portfolio, version, window, currency, strategist_key, blocks (weights), mix_start, m}. m keys: cagr, vol, mdd (worst fall), f10 (falls 10%+), wm (worst month), luw (longest underwater, months), ulcer, edge + spy_share (USD rows), edge_sgd_proxy + edge_sgd_usbills (SGD rows). 4 decimals. version: spy | research | ucits_rule | ibkr | twin.
schema.falls: {series_info, USD:{episodes, returns}, USD_in_SGD:{returns}, SGD:{episodes, returns}}; episodes [{peak, low, depth, inner, usd_vs_sgd}]; returns {series id: [one value per episode, null = not covered]}.
schema.same_pain_line: {USD|SGD|SGD_cash_proxy: {window: {spy_share [0..100 step 5], ulcer, cagr}}}. SGD = SPY + US T-bills both in SGD (U-shaped); SGD_cash_proxy = SPY in SGD + T-bill yield with no FX move.
schema.funds: Explorer list [{ticker, name, desc, category, group, where (lse|sgx|us_etf|us_mf|research), quote_ccy, teams, flag, first, cards:{USD|SGD:{window: {cagr, mdd, f10, ulcer, wm, edge (USD only)} | null}}, first_day_zero?, falls:{USD:[per falls.USD episode], SGD:[per falls.SGD episode]}}]. where_label in meta.where_label.
schema.teams: [{id, title_en/zh, question_en/zh, verdict_en/zh, audited, audit_corrections, audit_note_en/zh, findings:[{en, zh, source, where}], link, audit_link}]; *_zh fields are null for the front-end team to fill.

teams.question_en: Do defensive stock funds (min-vol, quality, dividend, staples, buffer, option income, Singapore stocks) cut drops?
teams.audit_note_en: 1 claim corrected (Singapore stocks' pain since 2020); 3 notes and 2 missing items added.

findings.en: Defensive stock funds softened ordinary dips but not crashes: in the Covid crash USMV fell 33.0% while SPY fell 33.7%.
Consumer staples (XLP) cut every crash it saw (at most 72% of SPY's loss in four crashes since 1999), but earned 8.0% a year since 2015 against 13.7% for SPY.
No defensive stock fund beat the same-pain yardstick in two of three separate periods (2008-14, 2015-19, 2020-26).
Buffer ETFs gave about what a cheap SPY + T-bill mix gave (BUFR 9.9% a year vs 9.8% since 2021-06); the option-income fund SVOL fell 33.5% in the 2025 dip while SPY fell 18.8%.
In SGD since 2008 the STI ETF (ES3.SI) earned 5.0% a year against 10.6% for SPY, with a deeper worst fall (-57.7% vs -48.1% for SPY in the team’s count; -48.6% on this page’s convention).

teams.question_en: Which bonds, cash and gold held up in SPY's falls, in USD and SGD?
teams.verdict_en: Pass, with one correction and added caveats
teams.audit_note_en: 1 claim corrected (T-bills in SGD rose in 9 of 9 falls, not 14 of 14); 3 caveats added.

findings.en: Only T-bills never failed: cash rose in all 14 of SPY's falls of 10%+ since 1993, but earned only 1.4% a year since 2008.
7-10 year Treasuries (IEF) rose in 7 of 9 SPY falls since 2007 (+20.2% in 2008-09) but lost 15.4% in 2022, when TLT lost 29.3%.

Since 2022 Treasuries have tended to move with stocks: on weekly returns IEF’s median correlation with SPY was +0.24 in 2022-2026 against -0.30 in 2003-2021 (audit check; daily medians -0.39 and +0.07).
findings.where: README.md, What we found 3; AUDIT.md concern 4

findings.en: Gold rose in 6 of 9 SPY falls since 2007 but fell 45.6% on its own in 2011-2015; high-yield bonds (HYG) lost money in all 9 falls.
For an SGD investor the US dollar rose against the SGD in each of the 9 SPY falls since 2007 (+0.3% to +6.7%), though it lost 0.6% a year since 2008.

teams.title_en: Trend following, hedge-fund-style funds and ready-made mixes
teams.question_en: Do managed-futures, hedge-fund-style and balanced funds cut drops?
teams.audit_note_en: 1 sentence corrected (BTAL as a 40% sleeve); 1 caveat added (balanced-fund winners depend on the start date).

findings.en: Managed-futures funds protected in slow bear markets, not sudden shocks: in 2022 all but WTMF rose (+14% to +48%) while SPY fell 24.5%; in Feb 2018 and Feb-Apr 2025 every one lost money.
On their own they are not calm: since 2015 AQMIX earned 4.6% a year with a pain score (Ulcer index) of 14.7, against 13.7% and 6.8 for SPY.
Next to 60% SPY, a 40% AQMIX sleeve beat holding less SPY by 1.5 points a year since 2010, but only thanks to 2020-2026.
Hedge-fund replication ETFs (QAI, HDG) lost in all 6 SPY falls since 2015 and trailed the same-pain yardstick by 4 to 8 points a year.
Balanced funds beat holding less SPY before 2015, not after; in 2020-2026 only PRPFX (+1.6) and BLNDX (+1.4) stayed ahead, and that depends on the start date.

teams.title_en: C30 for a Singapore investor on IBKR
teams.question_en: How did the tested C30 mix do when built from IBKR-buyable funds, in USD and SGD?
teams.audit_note_en: 2 rounding slips and 1 over-strong claim corrected; 3 caveats added.

findings.en: Built from CSPX.L, IB01.L, CBU0.L, IGLN.L and DBMF, C30 returned 9.7% a year from 2020-01-02 to 2026-10-27, the same as the research version, with a same-pain edge of +2.3 points (research: +2.5).
Its worst fall was deeper, -12.6% against -8.8%, mostly because DBMF lost 6.6% in the Covid crash while the trend rule gained 17.4%.
findings.where: README.md, What we found 2 (corrected in audit)

findings.en: In the three SPY falls since 2020 the IBKR version lost 11.7%, 7.1% and 4.8% while SPY lost 33.7%, 24.5% and 18.8%.
In SGD since 2008 C30 fell at most 8.9% (15.5% in USD); since 2020 the IBKR version was 1.4 points a year ahead of SPY plus an SGD-cash stand-in.
With London UCITS lines for four blocks, fund fees average about 0.22% a year (approximate) and only DBMF is US-listed.

teams.question_en: Synthesis: which low-drop portfolios suit a Singapore investor on IBKR, and how to hold them?
teams.verdict_en: Not audited (synthesis of the audited teams)
teams.audit_note_en: Not audited; it reproduces the tested C30 (9.71% a year) and the audited IBKR version (9.70%, edge +2.26) before reporting anything.

findings.en: All three model portfolios lost less than SPY in each of SPY's 9 falls since 2007 (research blocks, USD).
They trailed holding less SPY in calm 2015-2019 by 1.6 to 2.8 points a year, and beat it in 2008-2014 and 2020-2026.
Core (the pre-registered C30) returned 7.0% a year since 2008 with a worst fall of -15.5% and one fall of 10%+, against 11.2%, -52.3% and 8 falls for SPY.
Since 2020, with real IBKR funds, the models gave up 4.7 to 7.2 points a year of return compared with SPY.
Only Core was pre-registered and tested out of sample; Conservative and Growth were chosen after seeing the data (post-hoc).

estate_tax.rule_en: US-listed shares count as US assets for US estate tax. For a non-US person the exemption is about US$60,000 and the tax above it can reach about 40% (approximate). Irish UCITS funds and the Irish gold ETC are not US assets, so in these models only DBMF is exposed. Its holding passes US$60,000 when the whole portfolio passes US$60,000 / DBMF weight: about US$400,000 at 15% (Conservative, Growth) and US$343,000 at 17.5% (Core). An all-US-listed version would be exposed from the first US$60,000.

frictions.fx_conversion_en: IBKR converts SGD to USD for about 0.002% of the amount, minimum about US$2 (approximate).
frictions.withholding_en: Singapore has no US tax treaty: US-listed funds lose 30% of dividends; Irish UCITS funds pay 15% on US dividends inside the fund and nothing more (approximate).
frictions.rebalancing_en: Check monthly; rebalance a block more than 5 percentage points from target, and at least once a year. Monthly, quarterly and a 5-point band were within -0.2 to +0.6 points a year of each other (post-hoc).

caveats_en: The ingredients (gold, trend) were chosen after seeing how they behaved in 2020-2026; only the weights and stock share were chosen on 2005-2019 data.
Gold and trend had an unusually good test period; with gold's return cut to its earlier pace the edge falls from +2.5 to +0.9 points a year.
In calm 2015-2019 C30 earned 2.8 points a year less than the same-pain SPY + T-bill mix.
Seven years and three falls cannot prove a return edge; the drop results are more convincing.

fund_drops.summary_en: Of about 90 ETFs and funds, only PRPFX (the Permanent Portfolio fund, several different shock absorbers) beat ‘just hold less SPY’ in both windows (since Oct 2007 and since 2020).
